nominations.rationale: By extending the concepts of solid-state bandgaps to optics, they created materials that can trap and mold the flow of light. Their work has fundamentally changed nanophotonics and optical engineering.

nominations.discovery: for the prediction and discovery of correlated and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene
key_papers: Bistritzer and MacDonald, PNAS, 2011: Moire bands in twisted double-layer graphene
Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene superlattices
nominations.rationale: The realization that a slight rotational twist between atomic layers could generate completely flat electron bands and tunable superconductivity birthed the field of twistronics. This has provided an unprecedented experimental platform for studying strongly correlated quantum systems.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical discovery of the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the geometric phase, revealing the fundamental role of gauge potentials and topology in quantum mechanics
key_papers: Y. Aharonov and D. Bohm, Physical Review, 1959: Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory
M. V. Berry, Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences, 1984: Quantal Phase Factors Accompanying Adiabatic Changes
nominations.rationale: These theoretical breakthroughs fundamentally transformed our understanding of quantum mechanics by demonstrating that electromagnetic potentials have observable effects in field-free regions and that quantum systems retain a memory of their evolution through geometric phases. Their work paved the way for the modern topological revolution in condensed matter physics.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical formulation of cosmic inflation and the prediction of the quantum origin of cosmological structure
key_papers: A. H. Guth, Physical Review D, 1981: Inflationary universe: A possible solution to the horizon and flatness problems
A. D. Linde, Physics Letters B, 1982: A new inflationary universe scenario: A possible solution of the horizon, flatness, homogeneity, isotropy and primordial monopole problems
V. F. Mukhanov and G. V. Chibisov, JETP Letters, 1981: Quantum fluctuations and a nonsingular universe
nominations.rationale: Cosmic inflation provided a compelling theoretical mechanism to explain the homogeneity, isotropy, and flatness of the observable universe. Furthermore, their calculations of quantum fluctuations generated during inflation successfully predicted the primordial density perturbations that seeded all structure in the cosmos.

nominations.discovery: for foundational theoretical contributions to quantum information science, including quantum cryptography and quantum algorithms
key_papers: C. H. Bennett and G. Brassard, Proceedings of IEEE International Conference on Computers, Systems and Signal Processing, 1984: Quantum cryptography: Public key distribution and coin tossing
P. W. Shor, Proceedings of the 35th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science, 1994: Algorithms for quantum computation: discrete logarithms and factoring
nominations.rationale: Bennett and Brassard established the theoretical framework for secure quantum communication, while Shor's factoring algorithm demonstrated the exponential power of quantum computers. These visionary theoretical developments created the foundation for the entire modern field of quantum technology.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of strongly correlated physics and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene
key_papers: R. Bistritzer and A. H. MacDonald, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2011: Moire bands in twisted double-layer graphene
Y. Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene superlattices
Y. Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Correlated insulator behaviour at half-filling in magic-angle graphene superlattices
nominations.rationale: MacDonald and Bistritzer theorized that twisted layers of graphene at a specific magic angle would exhibit flat energy bands, a prediction spectacularly validated by Jarillo-Herrero's discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. This breakthrough catalyzed the new field of twistronics, offering a highly tunable platform for exploring strongly correlated quantum phases.

nominations.discovery: for theoretical and experimental breakthroughs in the control of electromagnetic waves using photonic crystals and metamaterials
key_papers: E. Yablonovitch, Physical Review Letters, 1987: Inhibited Spontaneous Emission in Solid-State Physics and Electronics
J. B. Pendry et al., Physical Review Letters, 1999: Magnetism from Conductors and Enhanced Nonlinear Phenomena
nominations.rationale: Yablonovitch conceptualized photonic crystals that manipulate light analogously to how semiconductors control electrons, while Pendry pioneered metamaterials that allow extreme control over the refractive index, including negative refraction and cloaking. Their visionary concepts have spawned entirely new branches of optics and photonics.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical prediction and experimental realization of negative index metamaterials
key_papers: Pendry et al., IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques, 1999: Magnetism from conductors and enhanced nonlinear phenomena
Smith et al., Physical Review Letters, 2000: Composite Medium with Simultaneously Negative Permeability and Permittivity
nominations.rationale: Metamaterials have revolutionized our understanding of electromagnetism, enabling unprecedented control over light and paving the way for cloaking devices and superlenses. This represents a true paradigm shift in optics and materials science, demonstrating that complex macroscopic structures can transcend the optical limits of their constituent atoms.

nominations.discovery: for the formulation of the hydrodynamic theories of active matter and flocking

Simha and Ramaswamy, Physical Review Letters, 2002: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations and Instabilities in Ordered Suspensions of Active Particles
nominations.rationale: Active matter extends statistical mechanics to systems where individual components continuously consume energy, capturing the complex collective behavior of everything from bacterial swarms to bird flocks. Their pioneering equations have created a vibrant new subfield of nonequilibrium physics that beautifully unites biology, soft matter, and complex systems.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of correlated insulator behavior and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
key_papers: Bistritzer and MacDonald, PNAS, 2011: Moire bands in twisted double-layer graphene
Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Correlated insulator behaviour at half-filling in magic-angle graphene superlattices
Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene superlattices
nominations.rationale: The discovery of moire quantum matter has opened an entirely new platform for investigating strongly correlated physics and high-temperature superconductivity. This breakthrough bridges complex systems and quantum condensed matter in an elegant, highly tunable way.

nominations.discovery: for the formulation of the Kuramoto model and foundational contributions to the physics of synchronization in complex systems
key_papers: Kuramoto, International Symposium on Mathematical Problems in Theoretical Physics, 1975: Self-entrainment of a population of coupled non-linear oscillators
Strogatz, Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena, 2000: From Kuramoto to Crawford: exploring the onset of synchronization in populations of coupled oscillators
nominations.rationale: The mathematical description of how coupled oscillators spontaneously synchronize has proven to be a universal concept, applicable to chemical waves, neural networks, and power grids. Their work perfectly encapsulates how simple rules give rise to deeply complex, emergent macroscopic phenomena across all disciplines of physics.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery of the geometric phase in quantum systems
key_papers: Berry, Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A, 1984: Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes
nominations.rationale: The Berry phase is a profound fundamental discovery that has influenced everything from optics to condensed matter, fundamentally underpinning the modern understanding of topological states of matter. It remains one of the most broadly applicable concepts in modern theoretical physics, demonstrating deep geometric connections in complex quantum systems.

nominations.discovery: for the invention and development of aberration-corrected electron microscopy
key_papers: Haider et al., Nature, 1998: Electron microscopy image enhanced
Rose, Optik, 1990: Outline of a spherically corrected semiaplanatic medium-voltage transmission electron microscope
nominations.rationale: Aberration correction removed the physical limits of electron lens resolution that had stood for decades. This enabled true sub-angstrom imaging of atomic lattices, revolutionizing materials science and solid-state physics.

nominations.discovery: for the theoretical prediction and experimental realization of metamaterials with a negative refractive index
key_papers: Pendry et al., Phys. Rev. Lett., 1999: Magnetism from conductors and enhanced nonlinear phenomena
Smith et al., Phys. Rev. Lett., 2000: Composite Medium with Simultaneously Negative Permeability and Permittivity
nominations.rationale: Their work demonstrated that artificially structured materials can circumvent classical electromagnetic limits. This discovery has profound implications for microscopy and optics through the concept of a perfect lens that surpasses the diffraction limit.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery and development of photonic crystals
key_papers: Yablonovitch, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1987: Inhibited Spontaneous Emission in Solid-State Physics and Electronics
John, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1987: Strong localization of photons in certain disordered dielectric superlattices
nominations.rationale: By engineering periodic dielectric structures that act as a bandgap for light, they created an entirely new paradigm for controlling photons. This has driven massive advancements in optoelectronics, optical fibers, and nanoscale light-matter interactions.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene and the founding of twistronics
key_papers: Cao et al., Nature, 2018: Unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle graphene superlattices
Bistritzer and MacDonald, PNAS, 2011: Moiré bands in twisted double-layer graphene
nominations.rationale: The ability to tune the electronic properties of two-dimensional materials merely by rotating them has opened a vast new playground for quantum materials. It allows unprecedented experimental control over strongly correlated electron systems and structural moiré patterns.

nominations.discovery: for the discovery of topological and geometric phase effects in quantum mechanics
key_papers: Aharonov and Bohm, Phys. Rev., 1959: Significance of Electromagnetic Potentials in the Quantum Theory
Berry, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A, 1984: Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes
nominations.rationale: Geometric phases have evolved from surprising theoretical insights into cornerstones of modern condensed matter physics. They fundamentally underpin our current understanding of quantum interference, electron transport, and topological phases of matter.
